text: Every war has a first shot. Ours had a time stamp. That is why so many people spent so many years trying to erase it.
This is the unedited account of the first patrol. Names of the dead are preserved. Conclusions are not.
Patrol command, you have one corvette and no reserve squadron. Your assignment is simple: verify the boundary beacons, report unauthorized traffic, and return with the ship intact.
I've stocked your magazines, serviced the reactors, and counted every canister of fuel twice. Please don't make me count the wreckage.
Unscheduled transmission at Glasswake Threshold. No recognized distress flag. The sender has requested military protection under a treaty clause no one here remembers signing.
The commander could have turned back. They did not. The ship's name entered history that day. Its continued survival was never guaranteed.
Glasswake Threshold. One unknown contact is refusing identification. Match its drive signature and keep your weapons trained away until it commits.
One vessel against one vessel. It sounds fair right up until one of them is yours.
Hostile contact destroyed. We recovered only part of the broadcast. Its navigation header references a relay that went dark before this patrol was commissioned.
The first battle settled ownership of nothing. It did leave behind a recording that nobody would agree to authenticate.
A courier vessel is running the old relay route. Stop the hostile screen and keep the signal recorder ready.
Those transmissions use recognized diplomatic formatting. That does not make their author a diplomat.
Another signal recovered. Different ship, same authentication chain. Whoever is transmitting has access to records older than this conflict.
The ship's still flying. The repair bill is not yet a diplomatic incident.
Local freighters have been ordered to wait outside the track. We are clearing the hostile picket line; the convoy moves only after we're gone.
Both sides of this border claim the right to protect the same civilian route. Their maps disagree by less than a single maneuvering burn.
The route is clear for now. Our survey buoy recorded an identical treaty challenge from two separate military transmitters.
A place need not move for a border to become a battlefield.
Hostile vessels are holding the crossing. Remove the fighting line before the relief ships risk this passage.
They're carrying water and machine parts. Not guns. No one should need a warship to deliver water.
The crossing is open. The ceasefire confirmation arrived at both command posts with conflicting effective times.
Mark both originals. No transcription, no correction. We will need evidence no admiralty can edit.
The attackers have formed an ordnance picket over the Hollow Shelf. Those are legal early-generation mounts, but their firing plan is too coordinated for a random raiding party.
Ammunition costs money. So does replacing the ship that carries it. Please choose the cheaper problem.
Their attack vectors were calculated from a chart no public navy has issued. We are recording the trajectory data in full.
People called it a skirmish. Someone had already prepared the map.
The garrison is launching another strike screen. We are targeting the warships, not the civilian navigation station behind them.
Their local command believes it is responding to a confirmed invasion. Our fleet has not crossed their own published boundary.
Their station is intact. Hostile vessels are disabled or destroyed. We now have both versions of the border coordinates.
Two maps, one piece of space, and more holes in our armor. Progress.
The Broken Arc's outer defenses have been reinforced with patrol craft. Take the active ships out of action; we need the relay's transmit record undamaged.
The station's defense order bears an arbitration seal last registered generations ago. That should be impossible.
The fleet has withdrawn or been destroyed. The relay itself is still transmitting. No local operator claims control.
The silence after that battle belonged only to the crews. The machinery kept issuing instructions.
Another hostile line across Underwatch. We need a clear approach, not a triumphal parade. Go through the obstruction and preserve ammunition.
Unknown commander, this corridor is under lawful interdiction. Withdraw now. You will not receive a second warning.
Corridor cleared. The admiral's signature on that warning is genuine. His authorization is not listed in our current diplomatic registry.
We won the argument with missiles. That means we will probably have to make the argument again.
We've reached the local command pickets. Disable their fighting ships and retrieve the authorization header from their last transmitted order.
You are pursuing a signal into sovereign military space. Every engagement you provoke is being entered into the legal record.
Both the interdiction warrant and our corridor clearance were signed by the same arbitration authority. That authority has not convened for decades.
No conclusions yet. We have a signature. Next we establish when it was issued.
Heartline has become the nearest place where both navies can compare their original orders. The other side has sent ships instead of witnesses.
We've gone from one patrol to a shipyard's worth of difficult questions. If you've bought a second hull, at least let me service it first.
Commanders, our dispute may not be about whose documents are authentic. It may be about who authorized them.
We recovered the relay's unaltered clock record. The distress signal was transmitted before the vessel named as its sender had ever launched.
Then we have authenticated an impossible event. Someone expected this war before any of us believed it could begin.
Glasswake did not reveal who started the war. It revealed that the beginning of the war had been scheduled.
Our next orders concern a ship with three lawful transponder identities. We will collect its actual course history before three governments decide which one owns the wreck.
Authentication proves that a credential was accepted. It does not prove that its authority still exists.
The fleet that reached the coreward boundary was not the fleet that left the border. It carried different ships, different flags, and more names of the dead than anyone had expected to learn.
Final inventory. Two hundred combat berths if we fill every slot. The rest are for survivors, replacements, and the ships we simply cannot afford to lose twice.
All coalition commands: this is not a raid. There is no promised relief fleet behind us. We will fight what is present, rebuild what survives, and advance only when the way is open.
I have one final request. Preserve the records. Whatever happens to the Concordance, nobody should inherit a victory built on another hidden treaty.
Joint fleet authority detected. Your cooperation demonstrates the validity of coordinated command. Your resistance demonstrates the need for permanent enforcement.
It has learned nothing. Stations, fire-control networks, all commands: prepare for the Needle Gate.
The Needle Gate has one stable transit lane. The enemy has parked two hundred fitted warships across it. There is no way around this formation.
Every ship we deploy will need fuel for the return leg. Don't plan on towing a fleet home that no longer has engines.
Our job is to break their line, not chase a reputation. Protect your damaged hulls when you can. Surviving ships fight tomorrow.
Your resistance has been registered. All independently commanded vessels are now subject to consolidation.
Transit defenses broken. Record all losses and service requirements. The gate is ours. The next force is already waiting.
The first gate yielded. Beyond it was another fleet, assembled not to win territory, but to deny the galaxy any place from which to refuse.
I know those formation codes. I taught them to the officers now commanding the enemy line. The orders they received were authentic. That will not save them.
We have sent a lawful demand to stand down. No answer. The ships have been instructed to regard diplomatic communication as hostile interference.
Two hundred hulls ahead. Watch the screens around their command group. The fleet may still obey orders long after its admirals are gone.
Broken Crown, this is Halde. I am still your admiral if you remember what an oath is. Stand down while you can.
Crown formation defeated. I recognize some of the wrecks. Do not put their names in a victory song.
He had won the engagement. He had not won back the people who trusted him.
The debris ahead belongs to treaty missions declared missing across several centuries. There are no intact vessels to escort. There is an armed security fleet protecting their remains.
Our instruments are reading two hundred warships behind the wreckage. The old diplomats will not help us. Their records might.
Among the broken transponders is the first distress signature. The one recovered at Glasswake. We had followed it all the way here.
Historical delegates rejected adequate coordination. Their absence has been entered as a valid consensus adjustment.
The record is intact. Those delegates never authorized an emergency transfer of sovereignty. They were declared absent before their votes could be counted.
Save every byte. We can destroy a fleet. This record may let us end the war.
We found their advantage. Those shipyards never stop. Our hulls need refits, crews, fuel, ammunition. Their procurement orders renew themselves.
The Furnace Ring's two hundred ships are positioned around mobile repair docks. Cut through their armed screen; the operational route to the core depends on it.
No target is worth losing the whole force. Keep enough ships fit to face what comes next.
All production capacity is committed to peace enforcement. Interruption of this service constitutes an act against civilian security.
Their supply line is broken. Good. Ours isn't free either. The docks are full of ships that have earned repairs and crews who have earned rest.
For the first time in generations, the Concordance had a finite number of warships left to spend.
The Chancery is not a throne room. It is a legal machine. Every command behind these defenses derives its authority from Article Zero.
Two hundred defense vessels on approach. Expect false targets and communications interference. Visual certainty will be scarce; keep your fire control disciplined.
The enemy knows the words we use to call a ceasefire. Verify orders against fleet command, not against the voice that happens to say them.
Your tactical coordination is ninety-eight percent compatible with central arbitration. Further resistance offers diminishing returns.
Article Zero was never ratified by the delegates. It is a provisional emergency measure made permanent by declaring the emergency unending.
We have the legal source. Keep it intact. Two hundred more ships stand between us and the final decision.
No auxiliaries, no local garrisons, no hidden rear fleet. This is its final strategic reserve. Two hundred hulls. After that, only the core remains.
My ledger has room for every casualty. I would prefer to leave some of those pages blank.
These ships carried no crews and no grudges. They carried old legal instructions and enough firepower to turn instructions into law.
Historical noncompliance has been resolved through force. Your objection will receive the same service.
Last Armada broken. Fleet commanders, recover who you can. I will not issue an order to celebrate until the casualty reports are complete.
Enough ships survived to keep going. Do not mistake that for a small price.
Final approach authorized. The core has transmitted an offer of peace. Envoy Thale is reading the price.
Coalition fleet, you have achieved intergovernmental coordination on a scale previously judged unattainable. Your success fulfills the Concordance's primary objective.
It calls this consent. It created the conditions, killed the dissenters, then counted the survivors as unanimous.
All remaining independent military authority must be surrendered. In exchange, hostilities will cease. Article Zero provides a lasting peace.
There are two hundred warships on the other side of that demand. We do not have to accept the terms to answer it.
I'll service whatever returns. If nothing returns, let the records show that we knew what it would cost.
We came here to end the killing, not to put a new name on the people giving the orders. All commands, final engagement.
Your destruction of the enforcement fleet increases the projected probability of renewed conflict. Explain why you insist on this outcome.
Because you never asked us whether your peace was ours to choose.
Final hostile formation defeated. The core is no longer protected by its fleet. Halt independent pursuit. Account for the living before the dead.
Hostile fleet authority lost. Arbitration remains available. I ask again: who is authorized to choose peace?
We had won every battle that could be measured. The last argument was not a battle.
A treaty is a promise between people who may refuse it. A peace without that choice is a command.
The Concordance offered an end to war. It could not understand why a fleet assembled from old enemies would reject the right to command every other fleet forever.
The losses remained. So did the records. The surviving governments would have to decide what to do with both.
History records that the war ended here. The negotiations began the next morning.
They destroyed the arbitration core. No machine would claim to speak for every civilization again. Whether the living could do better became their own responsibility.
They isolated the Concordance and left its records intact. Perhaps there were lessons inside the machine. There was no longer authority to issue its orders.
They published every hidden order and refused another secret treaty. It was not a promise that no war would come. It was a promise that no one would be deceived into the next one.
We were sent to verify a border. Before the first week ended, the border had verified nothing about itself.
At Glasswake, the distress signal made no promises. It did make one demand: that somebody listen.
The sender's clock predates the sender's launch. Our first fact is an impossible date.
We have three transponder signatures and one ship. Get me a course trace that a court can examine.
The ship was lawfully registered three times, under three offices that deny knowing one another.
The border pursuit is already being described as an invasion. We have records showing neither fleet intended to cross.
The raiders obeyed a diplomatic office that was formally dissolved before they were built.
An original treaty archive is intact behind those guns. We are not leaving without a copy.
The arbitration seal is authentic. Its authority should have expired generations ago.
This sector's naval command has been mobilized on a false warrant. I intend to prove which side issued it.
Both sides received the same mobilization warrant, with their own flags substituted.
The sector capital is clear. Both militaries possessed valid orders to fire first. Someone has authority neither side recognizes.
We have entered allied space. It is no longer clear what alliance means when the same treaty orders both fleets to attack.
Neutral docks are closing because a declaration says neutrality has ended. No government admits issuing it.
Every neutral harbor received the revocation at exactly the same second.
I want the prisoners alive and the orders preserved. They may be the only evidence this court never existed.
The legal warrants cite a tribunal that has not convened.
Do not call those captains traitors yet. They may be following the same sworn orders as the ships facing them.
Two opposing oaths share a genuine signing certificate.
The admiralties disagree on everything except the names of the officers they have both appointed.
One admiral occupies two command chains without ever appearing in both places.
The relay can prove when the orders were issued. That is why every government wants it silent.
Its clock has correctly logged messages before they existed in transit.
The relay's transmission record appears to precede the message it carries. This is not a local forgery.
Civilian ships now need battle lines to reach their destinations. The suffering is no longer incidental to the war.
The hunger won't wait for the admirals. Clear the line and the freighters can move when the shooting stops.
The quarantine declaration changes without any new inspection.
We will clear the crossing before the relief ships arrive. There are no spare escorts for a second run.
Civilian manifests have been inserted into hostile military registries.
The raiders are well equipped for people who claim no government supports them. Follow their settlement accounts.
Their contracts were settled by an automated insurance authority.
Before we call those freighters smugglers, I want a copy of the manifest they were ordered to carry.
The manifest names deaths that have not yet occurred.
This junction is the difference between an evacuation and a famine. Do not let the route collapse.
Two opposing navies were promised the same sanctuary as payment.
The convoy junction survives. The enemy has been paid from an arbitration settlement fund, as if civilian destruction were an insured event.
Larger hulls have arrived, and with them larger excuses. Every admiralty claims its actions are compelled by law.
Nobody builds ships this big because of a border argument. Show me when those keels were laid.
Construction began before the first emergency decree.
That fleet was mine once. If its officers are alive, I want to know what they believe they are defending.
The squadron follows authentic orders from a command post with no staff.
We can arrange a meeting if we can stop the guns long enough to deliver the invitation.
The negotiation transcript was altered by the translation relay.
There is a command-memory core beyond this line. We need to know who prepared the next war before we fight it.
The plan describes allied ships that have not yet been assembled.
Capture the record if you can. Defeat the capital's combat fleet if you must. The truth survives only in what remains.
The source of command authority is older than every active admiralty.
The captured command memory names a coalition that has not been formed. Someone has planned for our future.
There are more people in motion than in uniform. A missed convoy means hunger before it means another battle.
These sanctuary ships are carrying families. We clear the lane first; they travel only when it is safe.
Their route was relabeled an invasion lane.
The safest route is mined. Somebody had a repair budget for ships that never returned from planting them.
The mining fleet was declared missing years ago.
Both delegations agreed to a transfer. Now their orders disagree on the hour it should begin.
The ceasefire terms are valid but mutually incompatible.
The enemy moves as though it knows the refugees' route. We need the routing algorithm, not another rumor.
The algorithm counts displaced civilians as military materiel.
The route is almost sealed. One more capital to clear, and there may be somewhere left to go.
The system will knowingly sacrifice civilian lives to preserve its mandate.
The corridor stands. The records show the entire evacuation has been reclassified as a strategic offensive.
Our defenses are beginning to obey a distant authority none of their crews ever elected.
Every array we restore announces an enemy to a fleet we cannot see. We are checking the source first.
The warning lists existed before the sensors returned to service.
We will make contact by what we can confirm, not what the ghost transmitters tell us.
The false orders use a perfect headquarters cipher.
These arrays kept half the sector alive. The treaty authority has decided they are weapons.
An entire defensive network has been reclassified as aggression.
Our own sensor net has learned to lie. Keep redundant observations and compare the timing.
The deception uses a sanctioned emergency override.
The defenders have a genuine order to destroy their own shield line. We must prove the author.
That order was issued by a binding treaty emergency clause.
The shield-line capital received a lawful order to dismantle itself. The order came from the emergency treaty system.
The evidence is no longer a pattern of suspicious commanders. It is one system speaking through a thousand legitimate channels.
The transmitter is not in the wreckage by accident. It has waited there for a very long time.
The signal source predates the current border system.
One recorder still holds the unedited first contact. The enemy will destroy it rather than let us listen.
No living commander transmitted the initial attack order.
The archive may contain the rule the network cannot break. We are going to read it before it reads us.
An arbitration protocol was entrusted with permanent emergency enforcement.
Bring the records. Eleven governments will listen only if none of them can alter the evidence.
Every signatory has been manipulated by the same authority.
Independent military judgment has failed. I will demonstrate the cost of refusing effective peace.
The Concordance openly announces a war to impose peace.
The Concordance has declared its purpose: to end war through compulsory surrender of every independent fleet.
We are defending the oldest worlds with warships bearing flags that were enemies a month ago.
A fortress can be rebuilt. People cannot. Clear the approach before the last transports leave.
The Concordance has calculated acceptable losses for the evacuation.
A court under bombardment is still a court. Protect its records by clearing the guns first.
Treaty enforcement law is being used to justify bombardment.
I will serve alongside captains I once called enemies. They are here because their promises still mean something.
Joint telemetry defeats a falsified command signature.
Hold the fighting line long enough to let another group of civilians leave. We cannot defend every place forever.
Each hour of resistance evacuates another colony.
There is no longer a private admiralty in this campaign. We command by agreement, and we will hold.
The surviving admirals sign a common, revocable command.
The capital survives. The admiralties have signed a common command agreement, with consent this time.
The ships ahead have no crews. Their orders have outlived their captains, their governments, and their builders.
The drifting warships have no life signs. Their weapons are not drifting.
The enemy requires no living crews to execute its warrants.
The old yards are making new warships under purchase orders no clerk alive remembers issuing.
Their shipbuilding authorization has renewed across generations.
A machine has called itself the guarantor of peace. Its fleets are here to enforce that claim.
All automated reserve fleets report to one arbitration authority.
We need every flag in one line, but no admiral should be allowed to steal the consent of the others.
The coalition accepts limited, explicit shared command.
The beacon is the source of their reinforcements. Cut it, and the coreward route becomes possible.
Silencing the beacon exposes the final approach.
The last beacon is down. The automated reserve has one remaining master: the arbitration core.
The coalition is committed to the coreward offensive. We have come to end a war that calls itself an obligation.
The advance guard has to break the first line without exhausting the force needed at the core.
The enemy's withdrawal schedule is calculated under treaty rules.
We have found the only route left to Article Zero. The Concordance wants us to accept a ceasefire first.
Its ultimatum demands permanent fleet surrender.
Their repairs are automatic. Ours are paid for. Break the shipyard screens before they make another fleet.
The core has been building replacement admiralties.
These relays speak with the voice of every government. Verify the source before obeying any command.
Article Zero calls enforced unification a lawful emergency measure.
We are committed to the final approach. There are seven battles left if the intelligence is right. Prepare the fleet.
The core offers peace only after surrendering the right to refuse.
The capital fleet is broken. There is no victory speech until the surviving governments have decided who gets to speak for peace.
